players.product: distribution transformers (83.7% exported; US distribution-transformer market)

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report: H1 2026 revenue KRW 70,322,807,356, down 36.4% from KRW 110,560,391,292 a year earlier, and operating profit KRW 11,122,563,262, down 69.5% from KRW 36,475,931,347; Q2 2026 revenue KRW 35,649,312,266 (Q2 2025: KRW 60,357,879,475), Q2 operating profit KRW 5,234,467,739 (Q2 2025: KRW 20,407,513,412). Management attributes the drop to slower growth as global supply capacity stabilised and competition intensified, higher fixed costs from pre-emptive investment in product-line expansion, operating deleverage and US tariff measures

Order backlog (transformers etc.) KRW 141,580M at June 30, 2026: total orders KRW 211,903M (carried-over backlog plus H1 orders) less H1 deliveries KRW 70,323M. Open US supply contracts with Public Service Electric and Gas (PSE&G) for distribution transformers: the 12-23-2024 contract of USD 29,647,830 (USD 15,822,900 delivered cumulatively, USD 13,929,100 in H1 2026) and the 12-22-2025 contract of USD 35,982,250 (deliveries not yet started)

quarterly_data.signal: Suppliers: core and other raw materials KRW 24,929M (94.1% of H1 purchases) from POSCO and Woojin Electric (a 9.52%-owned associate; H1 purchases from Woojin KRW 3,596,265,770); merchandise (mould transformers) from Mijoo Powertech; outsourced core processing KRW 1,535M from Hyungil Electric. Silicon steel sheet price flat at KRW 4,180/kg; amorphous oil-immersed core (50kVA) KRW 607,760 vs KRW 637,320 in FY2025
quarterly_data.counterparty: POSCO, Woojin Electric, Mijoo Powertech, Hyungil Electric

quarterly_data.signal: Capex and growth plan: bought Daejeon plant 2 land and buildings on 03-31-2026 for KRW 40,000M, part of a 2026 investment plan of KRW 45,545M (land, buildings) for market and product-line expansion; H1 PP&E acquisitions KRW 45,731,609,677. Management plans to enter the medium and large transformer market: a 154kV high-efficiency power transformer and a 145kV dead-tank circuit breaker are under development; UL/cUL certification for three-phase pad-mount transformers up to 3,750kVA obtained 2025.11. Management expects US distribution-transformer competition to intensify and tariff effects to grow, and will focus on keeping existing customers and winning new markets

KEPCO sanction over a gas-insulated switchgear bid-rigging case: KRW 1,165M fine (Fair Trade Commission, 2025) and a 6-month bid-participation restriction (2025-07-18), now stayed while the company's lawsuit proceeds; the company says it no longer supplies the affected 170kV GIS and expects minimal revenue impact because transformer exports are its main sales
